Thanks for the renewal estimate you sent last week. We're close to sign-off internally, but a couple of infra questions came up from our SRE and procurement teams: how does Redwood handle short-duration traffic spikes if we commit to a 1.5M token/month reserved pool? Specifically:

- Is there a hard cap we can opt into to avoid unpredictable overruns?

Sarah — great questions, thanks. High-level summary below, and I attached a short matrix that compares the three options. Happy to walk through live.

1) On-demand spillover (soft overflow):
   - Behavior: When reserved pool is saturated, requests are routed to shared-host burst capacity (multi-tenant).
   - Pros: Minimal latency impact for short spikes; no need to provision large headroom.
   - Cons: Higher per-token cost for spilled traffic; subject to best-effort latency SLAs (no committed 99p).

2) Pre-purchased burst credits:
   - Behavior: You buy a block of burst tokens/GPU-hours billed upfront at a discount. Spikes consume credits first.
   - Pros: Predictable max cost for known spike patterns; better latency than pure on-demand since we reserve capacity when credits are being used.
   - Cons: Requires forecasting and upfront spend.

3) Hard cap (strict overflow limit):
   - Behavior: Once the reserved pool + purchased burst is exhausted, excess requests are throttled or queued depending on your routing policy.
   - Pros: Strong cost predictability.
   - Cons: Possible user-facing latency/errors during large sustained spikes.

Throughput guarantees: For Dedicated pools we publish p50/p90 token throughput baselines per GPU shape; a contract-level 99p throughput SLA is available as an add-on if you commit to a 12-month reserved capacity with a minimum pool size (we can include an explicit tokens/sec target and remediation credits). For your size (current usage profile attached) we can propose a 99p target and include a fallback model variant to preserve latency if primary model stalls.

I've attached 'burst-policy-comparison.xlsx' with numbers and a draft order form 'redwood-dedicated-order-form.pdf' that includes an optional burst credits line item.

If helpful I can schedule a 30-minute call with our SRE/solutions lead to map your monthly patterns to the right combination (soft overflow + modest burst credits is what I normally recommend).

Thanks,

Hi all — following up with proposed contract language and operational guardrails. Draft snippets below you can drop into the service schedule.

1) Overflow behavior (soft overflow default):
   "Redwood will route excess requests to its multi-tenant burst capacity when a Customer's Reserved Pool is saturated. Such burst capacity is provided on a best-effort basis and is billed at the Provider's on-demand burst rate. The Provider does not guarantee latency or throughput for traffic served from multi-tenant burst capacity."

2) Prepaid burst credits:
   "Customer may purchase Burst Credits valid for the Contract Term. Burst Credits will be drawn before on-demand billing and expire at the end of the Contract Term unless otherwise agreed. Unused Burst Credits are non-refundable."

3) Hard cap toggle and emergency freeze:
   "Customer may enable a Hard Cap at any time to limit aggregate monthly consumption to the Reserved Pool plus pre-purchased Burst Credits. When Hard Cap is enabled, excess requests will be rejected with an HTTP 429 (Rate Limit Exceeded). Provider will not serve excess traffic beyond the cap unless Customer explicitly authorizes overage in writing."

4) Spike cost protection clause (procurement ask):
   "Provider will not invoice charges for any single hourly spike that exceeds 3x the Customer's historical peak hourly consumption (measured over the prior 90 days) unless Customer provides prior written approval. Provider and Customer may mutually agree to a one-time exception for an identified event."

Operational notes:
- We recommend enabling soft overflow + a small block of burst credits equal to 10% of your monthly tokens to cover typical diurnal spikes.
- For major launches, flip Hard Cap OFF and rely on burst credits + pre-warned capacity top-up.

If those clauses look good I can have Legal produce a side letter and we can incorporate it in the order form.

Best,
